text:
The `laravel/framework` package is currently in its **13th major iteration**, with the latest stable release being **v13.34.0**. Laravel has moved away from dedicated Long-Term Support (LTS) versions, opting instead for a consistent support policy across all major releases. Looking ahead, Laravel **14** is actively under development and is anticipated for release in early **2027**.

### The Current Stable Release: Laravel 13.x

The latest stable version of the `laravel/framework` package is **v13.34.0**, released on **September 29, 2026** [1][2]. This version, part of the Laravel 13.x series, mandates a minimum PHP version of **^8.3** [1][3]. Laravel 13 itself was initially launched on **March 17, 2026** [4][3].

Recent updates within the 13.x branch, such as v13.34.0, introduced enhancements like tracking job durations in `JobProcessed` events and improved notifications for jobs nearing timeout. Other updates in this series have included features like a Mercure broadcast driver, a read-through filesystem, and advancements in image processing [2][5].

### The Discontinuation of Long-Term Support (LTS)

Laravel no longer provides specific Long-Term Support (LTS) releases, a change that was implemented after Laravel 6 [4][6]. Instead, all major Laravel versions, including Laravel 13, adhere to a standardized support policy. This policy guarantees **18 months of bug fixes** and **two years of security fixes** from their release date [4][7].

For Laravel 13, bug fixes are scheduled until **September 17, 2027**, and security fixes will continue until **March 17, 2028** [8][3]. This approach ensures a predictable and consistent maintenance window for all major releases.

### The Next Generation: Laravel 14 in Development

Laravel 14 is the forthcoming major version and is currently under active development on the `master` branch of the `laravel/framework` repository [9][10]. Its release is projected for **Q1 2027** [9][11][12]. A key requirement for Laravel 14 will be a minimum PHP version of **8.4**, primarily driven by its dependency on Symfony 8.0 components [9][10]. Developers are advised to target PHP **8.5** for new projects, as PHP 8.4 will already be in security-fix-only mode by Laravel 14's expected release [10].

Anticipated features for Laravel 14, based on the `master` branch, include a new `Route::query()` helper for the HTTP `QUERY` method, an `authorize()` shorthand method on the user model, and an enhanced `report()` helper that accepts an optional context array [9][10]. Following the standard support policy, Laravel 14 is expected to receive bug fixes until **Q3 2028** and security updates until **Q1 2029** [9].

### Summary of Laravel's Release Approach

Laravel maintains a predictable annual release cycle, typically launching a new major version in the first quarter of each year [4][7]. This consistent schedule, combined with a uniform 18-month bug fix and 2-year security fix policy for all major versions, allows developers to plan upgrades and maintain their applications effectively while benefiting from continuous innovation delivered through weekly minor releases [4].

sources.title: framework/CHANGELOG.md at 13.x · laravel/framework · GitHub
claims: The Laravel framework's CHANGELOG.md for the 13.x branch details releases from v13.34.0 (2026-09-29) down to v13.0.0 (2026-03-17).
Release v13.34.0 on 2026-09-29 includes updates such as including duration in JobProcessed event, notifying jobs of timeouts, and adding a --queue option to queue:flush.
Release v13.33.0 on 2026-09-22 includes updates such as dropping restart_syscalls from pcntl_signal in Worker and adjusting when password hash is stored for authenticated sessions.
Release v13.32.0 on 2026-09-15 includes updates such as allowing enums in queue pause/resume methods and adding copyToDisk & moveToDisk to FilesystemAdapter.
Release v13.31.0 on 2026-09-08 includes updates such as adding totalSize method to Queue and restoring the container instance after route:cache boots a fresh application.
Release v13.30.1 on 2026-09-01 includes updates such as adding connection and queue to WorkerStopping and adding insertOrIgnoreReturning() to the Eloquent builder passthru.
Release v13.30.0 on 2026-09-01 includes updates such as outputting the worker stop reason in queue:work and supporting Microsoft SQL Server DSN connection strings.
Release v13.29.0 on 2026-08-25 has no specific changes listed in the provided changelog snippet.
Release v13.27.0 on 2026-08-25 includes updates such as preventing duplicate scoped instance registrations and adding refreshForUpdate() method to Eloquent models.
Release v13.26.1 on 2026-08-18 reverts a change related to orWhereKey and orWhereKeyNot.

sources.title: Laravel Releases: Latest Version (13.x), Changelog & Release Notes
claims: Laravel 13.34 counts worker crashes toward maxExceptions, notifies interruptible jobs before a timeout, and adds job durations to JobProcessed.
Laravel 13.33 adds tags to Cache::memo(), a Refreshes attribute for generated columns, AsCollection::nullable(), and inplace() index migrations.
Laravel 13.32 adds a Mercure broadcast driver, Storage::copyToDisk() and moveToDisk(), and enum support in queue pause/resume.
Laravel 13.31 adds Queue::totalSize() to count every job on a connection and a JobInterrupted event.
Laravel 13.27 masks query bindings in exception messages, adds whereBinary() for case-sensitive lookups, refreshForUpdate(), and a Cloud facade.
Laravel 13.26 adds a read-through filesystem driver, debounced queued event listeners, Queue::forward() routing, and new process testing helpers.
Laravel 13.25 adds queue:pause --all across every connection and runs artisan dev in a tabbed terminal UI.
Laravel 13.24 adds dominant color detection and HEIC support to the image API, a modelKeys() query builder method, and an array_keys validation rule.
Laravel 13.23 adds a monthly log rotation driver and SES tenant support in the SES v2 mail transport.
Laravel 13.22 adds a #\[BindWhen\] attribute for conditional container bindings and DNS lookup faking for validation rules.

sources.title: Laravel 14: What We Know So Far and How to Get Ready
claims: Laravel 14 is expected in Q1 2027.
Laravel 14 will require PHP 8.4 as a minimum version.
The PHP 8.4 minimum requirement for Laravel 14 is due to Symfony 8.0, which was released on November 27, 2025, and requires PHP 8.4.
The `master` branch of `laravel/framework` shows that all Symfony components are pinned to `^8.1.0`, removing the fallback for Symfony 7.4, which makes PHP 8.3 unresolvable.
PHP 8.4's active support ends on December 31, 2026, which is before Laravel 14 is expected to ship in Q1 2027.
PHP 8.5 is recommended as the target version, as it is supported by Laravel 13 and remains in active support through the end of 2027.
The `master` branch of `laravel/framework` shows a new routing helper `Route::query()` for the HTTP QUERY method.
The `master` branch of `laravel/framework` shows an authorization shorthand `$user->authorize()` that moves the entry point onto the user model.
The `report()` helper on the `master` branch gains a context array as an optional second argument.
The `master` branch of `laravel/framework` adds `Storage::fake('ondemand')` for on-demand disks in tests.
